3.summary: The Registrar of Companies can remove a company name from the official register on its own. However, certain companies like listed companies, those with pending court cases, or those holding public deposits cannot be removed. The Registrar must send a written notice to the company directors and give them time to reply.
points: The Registrar of Companies may remove a company name from the register on its own accord.
Listed companies, vanishing companies, and companies with pending court prosecutions or inspections cannot be removed.
Companies with outstanding public deposits or pending charges cannot be removed.
The Registrar must send a written notice to all directors via registered or speed post.
The company and its directors have thirty days to send representations and documents against the proposed removal.
3.example: The Registrar of Companies wants to remove Apex Trade Private Limited from the official register. The Registrar sends a written notice in Form STK 1 to all directors of Apex Trade Private Limited by speed post. The notice explains why the Registrar wants to remove the company name. The directors now have thirty days from the date of the notice to send their reply, along with any relevant documents, to oppose this action.

terms.meaning: An official appointed by the government to handle company registrations and records.
Companies whose shares are traded on a stock exchange.
A process of settling an offence by paying a fine or complying with rules to avoid further legal action.

3.watch: Even though the Registrar starts the removal, certain protected categories of companies can never be removed under this rule.

4.summary: This rule explains how a company can apply to remove its name from the official register. The company must fill out a specific form, pay a fee, and clear past financial statements and annual returns. Certain types of companies also need special permission or extra documents like bonds and accounts.
points: Applications to remove a company name must be filed in Form No. STK-2 with a fee of ten thousand rupees.
A company must file all overdue financial statements and annual returns up to the year it stopped doing business before applying.
Companies dealing with finance, insurance, or other regulated activities must include a no objection certificate from their regulatory authority.
The application must include an indemnity bond, a recent statement of accounts certified by a Chartered Accountant, an affidavit by every director, and details of any pending court cases.
4.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited decided to close down its business operations permanently. To do this, the company needed to remove its name from the official register. The directors gathered all the necessary papers, including a statement of accounts certified by a Chartered Accountant showing the company's assets and liabilities. They filled out Form STK-2, attached the required fee of ten thousand rupees, and submitted the complete application to the Registrar for processing.

terms.meaning: The government official who keeps records of companies.
A legal paper where someone promises to pay for any future losses or claims.
A written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence.

4.watch: A company cannot file the removal application if the Registrar has already issued a notice for publication to remove the company's name.

7.summary: This rule explains how public notices are published when a company's name is about to be removed from the official register. The notice is shared online, in the Official Gazette, and in two local newspapers. The authorities also inform tax departments so they can raise any objections.
points: Notices are published on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs website, in the Official Gazette, and in English and local language newspapers.
Companies applying themselves must also keep the application on their own website until it is decided.
The Registrar informs tax authorities, who have thirty days to send objections or be presumed to have none.
7.example: Asha Textiles Private Limited applied to remove its name from the official register. Following the rules, the Registrar published a public notice in an English newspaper and a local language newspaper circulating in the State where the company's office is located. Simultaneously, the Registrar sent an intimation letter to the local Income-tax authorities asking for any objections within thirty days. Since the tax authorities did not reply within this thirty-day period, the Registrar presumed they had no objections to the removal of the company's name.

terms.meaning: An official government publication used to share public legal notices.
The local language spoken by the ordinary people in a particular region or area.
The government office that handles company registrations and records.

7.watch: People often confuse the thirty-day limit for tax authorities with deadlines for other general public notices.

9.summary: This rule explains how the government official makes it public when a company's name is removed from the official records. The official publishes a notice in the Official Gazette and on the website of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. This step shows that the company has been dissolved.
points: The Registrar must publish a notice in the Official Gazette.
The notice must be in Form STK 7.
The same notice must be placed on the official website of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
9.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited reached the end of its business journey. The Registrar decided to remove the company's name from the official register. To make this final, the Registrar published a notice in the Official Gazette using Form STK 7. At the same time, the notice was uploaded to the official website of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs so everyone could see that Meera Textiles Private Limited was now dissolved.

terms.meaning: The government official who keeps track of companies.
An official government publication used to share public notices.
The official closing or ending of a company.

9.watch: People often confuse the removal of the company's name with an ordinary business closure, but this rule specifically deals with the official publication of that removal.

10.summary: This rule deals with old applications or pending proceedings for closing down a company that were filed before the current rules started. If these old requests were kept on hold because information or documents were missing, they will be finished using the older rules once the needed details are given. The text mostly focuses on handling these past pending cases based on older laws.
points: Old applications or pending proceedings filed before the new rules will be processed after missing information is submitted.
The handling of these specific pending cases follows the rules made under the older Companies Act, 1956.
The process applies only if the authority is satisfied with the submitted information or document.
10.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited had filed an old application for striking off its name before the current rules began. The Registrar of Companies kept the file pending because a specific document was missing. Once Meera Textiles Private Limited submitted the required document to the satisfaction of the authority, the pending proceeding was handled in accordance with the rules made under the Companies Act, 1956.

terms.meaning: The government authority that keeps records of companies.
Removing the name of a company from the official register.

10.watch: People might confuse these old transition rules with the brand new application process under current forms.

1.summary: This rule gives a short name to the set of rules used for removing company names from the official register. It also tells us when these rules start to apply. Because the text is very short, it only explains the title and the start date of the rules.
points: The rules are called the Companies (Removal of Names of Companies from the Register of Companies) Rules, 2016.
They start working on the date they are published in the Official Gazette.
1.example: A group of officers at Acme Logistics Private Limited wants to know when the new rules about removing company names from the official register officially start. They check the government publication date. According to the rule, the rules become active on the exact day they are published in the Official Gazette.

terms.meaning: The official government newspaper or publication used to announce public notices and laws.
The official list or record where active companies are registered.

1.watch: Do not confuse the name of the rules with the date they actually start, which depends on their publication.

2.summary: This rule gives basic meanings for words used in the specific company removal rules. It tells us that the word Act refers to the Companies Act, 2013. It also explains that any words not explained here will take their meaning from the main Act or other specified rules.
points: The term Act means the Companies Act, 2013.
Form or e-Form means a paper or electronic form attached to these rules.
Words not defined here take their meanings from the Act or the 2014 definition rules.
2.example: When Meera Textiles Private Limited wants to remove its name from the official register, it looks at the official rules. The company fills out an e-Form as mentioned in the rules. Since the rules use terms that are not fully explained inside this specific section, the directors check the main Companies Act, 2013, to understand those terms properly, just as this rule allows them to do.

terms.meaning: An electronic form connected to the rules.
The Companies Act, 2013.

2.watch: Do not assume terms unique to these rules have different meanings than they do in the main Act.

5.summary: This rule explains how to sign the application to remove a company name from the register. An authorized director must sign the form. If that director does not have a digital signature, they must sign a physical copy by hand and attach it to the online submission.
points: The application form must be signed by a director authorized by the Board.
If the director lacks a digital signature, they must sign a physical copy manually.
This signed physical copy must be attached when uploading the main form.
5.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wants to remove its name from the register of companies. The board of directors authorizes director Ramesh to sign the application form. Since Ramesh does not have a registered digital signature certificate, he fills out a physical copy of the form and signs it by hand. Ramesh then attaches this manually signed physical copy to the main digital form, STK 2, before uploading it.

terms.meaning: An official electronic key used to sign documents securely online.
The specific official form used to apply for removing a company name.

5.watch: People often confuse signing digitally with signing by hand, but manual signatures are only allowed for the physical copy attachment when a digital signature is missing.

6.summary: This rule explains that the application form to remove a company name must be certified by a qualified professional. Specifically, it must be signed and verified by a practicing professional like a Chartered Accountant, Company Secretary, or Cost Accountant. This ensures that the document is checked by an expert before submission.
points: Form STK 2 is the official form used for the process.
The form must be certified by a professional.
Allowed professionals are a whole time practicing Chartered Accountant, Company Secretary, or Cost Accountant.
6.example: Meera Textiles Private Limited decided to close its business and applied to remove its name from the official register using Form STK 2. Before submitting the form to the authorities, the directors asked Mr. Sharma, a Chartered Accountant in whole time practice, to review and certify the document. Mr. Sharma checked the details and signed it as required by the rule, ensuring the application met the proper certification standards.

terms.meaning: Checked, verified, and officially signed by an authorized expert.
Working actively and full-time in a professional practice rather than having another job.

6.watch: People often get confused about which professionals are allowed to sign this form.

8.summary: This rule explains what foreign nationals and non-resident Indians must do with their indemnity bond and declaration. These documents must be legally verified through notarisation, appostilisation, or consularisation. The text does not mention any related sections of the Companies Act, 2013.
points: Applies to foreign nationals and non-resident Indians.
Applies to the indemnity bond and declaration.
The documents must be notarised, appostilised, or consularisation.
8.example: John, a non-resident Indian living abroad, wants to close his company, Apex Global Private Limited, under the removal of names rules. To do this, he prepares an indemnity bond and a declaration as required by the law. Since he is outside the country, John must ensure that both his indemnity bond and declaration are properly notarised, appostilised, or consularised before submitting them.

terms.meaning: A legal written promise to pay for any losses or damages.
A formal official statement made by a person.
An Indian citizen who lives outside of India.

8.watch: Do not assume any specific country laws apply beyond the required verification methods mentioned.
